'''Joanne Elliott''' (December 5, 1925 – March 5, 2023) was an American mathematician who specialized in [[potential theory]],{{r|areas}} who was described as a "disciple" of her co-author, [[probability theory|probability theorist]] [[William Feller]].{{r|halmos}} She was also a [[professor]] of mathematics at [[Rutgers University]].{{r|areas}}

==Early life and education==
Elliott was born on December 5, 1925, in [[Providence, Rhode Island]],{{r|wbm}} and graduated from [[Brown University]] in 1947.{{r|wbm}}
She completed her Ph.D. at [[Cornell University]] in 1950, as part of a handful of "outstanding graduate students" working at Cornell in the post-World-War-II decade.{{r|cornell}} Her dissertation, ''On Some Singular Integral Equations of the Cauchy Type'', was supervised by [[Harry Pollard (mathematician)|Harry Pollard]].{{r|mgp}}

==Career and later life==
After a year at [[Swarthmore College]], she worked at [[Mount Holyoke College]] as an assistant professor from 1952 until 1956, when she moved to [[Barnard College]].{{r|wrut}} In 1958, she was the supervisor of [[Doris Stockton]]'s doctorate at [[Brown University]].{{r|brown}} In 1961, as an associate professor at Barnard, she was funded by the [[National Science Foundation]] to visit the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] for postdoctoral research.{{r|postdoc}} She also worked at the [[Institute for Defense Analyses]] in Princeton in the early 1960s.{{r|halmos}}

She came to [[Rutgers University]] in 1964, at a time when Rutgers had a much higher number of female faculty than many mathematics departments then or later.{{r|weibel}} Among her graduate students at Rutgers was [[Edward R. Dougherty]], later a distinguished professor of electrical engineering at [[Texas A&M University]].{{r|mgp}} She chaired the Rutgers mathematics department from 1974 to 1977.{{r|weibel}} Elliott retired from Rutgers in 1991, in a year in which the university was cutting costs by offering early retirement to its employees.{{r|weibel}}

Elliott died in [[Titusville, New Jersey]] on March 5, 2023, at the age of 97.{{r|obit}}
